conviction_note: Small negative: the print turns on the Q4 guide, management itself flagged Q4 memory uncertainty and the name sold 6 of its last 7 prints (including above-consensus guides). Against that, the 27% drawdown is the semiconductor tape (SOX -24% over the same window, AMBA beta about 2.4), the option skew pays for upside and the stock sits at its 52-week low. So p_up is 46, not lower. abs_move 15 sits above the indicative 12.7% implied move: the straddle quote is 52% wide, the name's own median reaction is 16.8%, and the SOX is moving 7-12% a day this week. The findings sum (-1.5) and the scaled number (-1.2) agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 FY27 revenue $119.4-119.9M and non-GAAP EPS $0.31-0.32. Two agreeing estimate sources: LSEG via Investing.com, $0.31 / $119.44M (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/ambarella-earnings-on-deck-as-ai-chip-transition-faces-test-93CH-5048515, 2026-11-24); Earnings Whispers, $0.32 / $119.9M, whisper $0.37 (https://finviz.com/news/423396/ambarellas-physical-ai-pitch-meets-a-margin-inventory-and-memory-test, 2026-11-16). The revenue consensus equals the company's guide midpoint ($115-124M, GM 59-60%, opex $56.5-59.5M; https://finviz.com/news/388851/ambarella-inc-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results). Benzinga's $0.22 EPS is an outlier and is disowned. No sourced Q4 (Jan-27) revenue consensus was found. Management's anchors for Q4 are 'regular seasonality' barring memory impact and FY27 growth of 10-15%. Q4 FY26 was guided about -6% sequential at the midpoint. FY27 at 12.5% implies Q4 near $108M if Q3 prints at the midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 4.7M shares, 10.5% of shares outstanding, 2.6 days to cover (settlement 2026-11-13, down 1.4% month on month; https://equibles.com/stocks/amba/summary). It was 12.9% of float and 2.3 days in early October. That is elevated but not crowded. Skew_25d is -6.92 vol points (upside paid); put/call OI is 0.23; total OI is only 4,044 and the ATM spread is 52% of mid, so the implied move (12.67%) is indicative only. Tape: -27.2% over 20 days, -8.75% over 5 days, 0.4% above the 52-week low, and -12.4% intraday on the print day (55.56 to 48.69) while the SOX was about -7.3% (8,886 against 9,588; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/%5ESOX?range=1mo&interval=1d). Institutional ownership is 82%. T. Rowe Price held 7.6% and Vanguard 7.0% at 2026-09-30.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide carries a flagged downside risk. On the Q2 call (2026-09-03) management said Q2 and Q3 saw little memory impact, but Q4 visibility is less certain while it 'works with customers to secure enough memory'. CEO Wang said Q4 should show 'regular seasonality' only 'barring any memory impact'. The last comparable Q4 guide (Nov 2025) was $97-103M against a $106.5M Q3, about -6% sequential at the midpoint. A memory-constrained Q4 guide meaningfully below roughly $110M would land below FY27's reaffirmed 10-15% growth midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has driven this name's prints and they have been sold. Nov 2025 Q4 guide $97-103M, ABOVE the $95.6M consensus, after a beat: -18.78% (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/11/26/why-ambarella-stock-just-crashed). May 2026 in-line Q2 guide: -21.41%. Feb 2026: -14.89%. Sep 2026 in-line Q3 guide: -0.77%. Six of seven prints were down; the only rise was +16.78% on a raised FY outlook (Aug 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The memory caveat is in the wire previews (Earnings Whispers 2026-11-16) and the stock is at its 52-week low. But the 27% drawdown tracks the SOX (-24% from Oct 28) rather than a name-specific de-rating, and Q3/FY estimates were flat over 60 days (Investing.com). If the market had priced a Q4 memory cut, revisions would show it, and the skew would not pay for upside (-6.9).
findings.independence: Dahua's price-adjustment notice cites supply constraints and price rises in SoCs, DRAM/NAND and PCBs for cameras (https://www.dahuasecurity.com/Japan/newsEvents/DahuaNotice/1518). That is camera-industry corroboration of cost pressure on Ambarella's end customers, but undated in the snippet and not a volume figure. The preview flags the same risk from a different author (https://finviz.com/news/423396/ambarellas-physical-ai-pitch-meets-a-margin-inventory-and-memory-test).

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue print is likely at or slightly above the $119.5M midpoint. Management said in September it expected little memory impact in Q3 and that Q3 growth would be led by Physical AI demand. The company has a documented conservative-guidance habit: it delivered 37% FY26 growth after talking mid-to-high teens (Cantor conference, March 2026). Possible customer pull-ins ahead of memory-driven cost increases would also favour Q3. But recent beats were tiny: Q2 $108.1M against $107.8-108.0M, Q1 $100.4M against $100.2M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats have not paid. Q3 FY26 beat by 2.3% on revenue and fell 18.8%; Q2 FY27 beat narrowly and fell 0.8%; Q1 FY27 beat narrowly and fell 21.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The whisper of $0.37 against $0.31-0.32 consensus already expects a beat. Filed because a top-of-range print ($124M) is what the whisper needs, and recent beats have been only 0.2-0.3%.
findings.independence: The Q2 call commentary on Q3 (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262150875-tradingkey) is a different document but the same management. Himax saw customers accelerate purchases ahead of rising memory prices in H1 (https://finviz.com/news/416607/himax-technologies-inc-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-provides-fourth-quarter-2026-guidance), a peer analogue for pull-ins and a proxy only.

findings.finding: The pre-print drawdown is sector-driven, not idiosyncratic. AMBA fell from $66.27 (Oct 28) to $48.69 intraday on Nov 24 (-26.5%), while the SOX fell from 11,684 to 8,886 (-24%) over the same days. Today AMBA is -12.4% against SOX -7.3%. With a 2.36 beta, AMBA has not underperformed what the sector implies. Meanwhile the skew pays for upside (-6.9 vol points, put/call OI 0.23) and short interest is about 10.5% of shares outstanding. So expectations into the print were reset by the tape rather than by company news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent. The prior prints came off higher bases (e.g. near the $94-97 high before May 2026). The Sep 2026 print, made with the stock already well off its highs, moved only -0.77%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about what IS priced. A low bar after a sector crash would show up as upside skew and calls bid, which is what the baseline shows. Tomorrow's sector tape (SOX swinging 7-12% a day) can swamp it either way.
findings.independence: SOX daily closes from a separate series: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/%5ESOX?range=1mo&interval=1d. The skew and put/call figures come from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Gross margin is under test. Q2 non-GAAP GM was 59.3%, below the guide midpoint, sliding from 59.9% the prior quarter and 60.9% a year earlier. Q3 is guided 59-60%, with rising supply-chain costs that management says it will pass through. A print at the low end, or a lower Q4 GM guide, would hit the 'quality of the beat'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Nov 2025 a one-point GM slip to 59.6% was cited alongside the -18.8% reaction despite the beat (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/11/26/why-ambarella-stock-just-crashed).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The guide already sits at 59-60%. It is filed because the trend is down three quarters running and the pass-through claim is untested.
findings.independence: The Q2 release confirms the 59.3% figure and the 59-60% guide (https://finviz.com/news/388851/ambarella-inc-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results). Same company source.

findings.finding: Inventory and cash flow are weak. Days of inventory were 157 at Q2 against 76 a year earlier and 145 the prior quarter, although inventory dollars fell 4% sequentially. FCF was negative for two quarters on IP license payments and inventory. Cash and securities were $272.3M against $277.8M in Q1 and $312.6M before that. Days rising again into a soft Q4 guide would read as a demand miscalculation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. This is a secondary line in prior reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. It is in the Earnings Whispers preview. Filed small because it matters only together with the Q4 guide.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview repeats the 157 versus 76 days figure (https://finviz.com/news/423396/ambarellas-physical-ai-pitch-meets-a-margin-inventory-and-memory-test). The Q1 cash figure is from Zacks (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2929075/ambarella-s-q1-earnings-meet-estimates-revenues-rise-on-auto-strength).

findings.finding: Arlo, a consumer security-camera OEM in Ambarella's IoT end market, reported on 2026-11-05 (after Ambarella last spoke). It guided Q4 revenue to $137-147M (midpoint $142M) against a $140.3M consensus, despite flagging memory cost increases. That is evidence that consumer camera volumes were not being cut for Q4 at least at one OEM.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific history of AMBA trading on Arlo read-throughs.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer read-through few previews connect to AMBA. But it is one OEM; I have not confirmed Arlo is a current Ambarella SoC customer; and memory affects Arlo's margin rather than its volume.
findings.independence: Proxy only. A second account of the Arlo guide calls it in line rather than above (https://finviz.com/news/418098/arlo-tops-consensus-but-misses-the-whisper-as-slowing-arr-growth-collides-with-a-bold-2027-target).

findings.finding: Auto peers guided Q4 down after Ambarella last spoke. On 2026-10-29 Mobileye guided Q4 EyeQ orders to 8.8-8.9M units against 9.5M in Q3 (about -7% sequential). Himax (early Nov) guided Q4 down 22-26% sequential on an abrupt China auto order correction. Ambarella's auto business hit a record in Q2, driven by commercial vehicles and new China in-cabin Tier-1 wins. Net of the rest of the company: IoT is the larger segment and grew in Q2, so this is a proxy on a minority segment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history. In Q2 auto grew slightly faster than IoT.
findings.why_not_priced: These are peer prints dated after Ambarella's September guidance. If the market had applied them, Q4 estimates would have come down, but Investing.com reports estimates flat over 60 days. Ambarella's auto mix (commercial vehicle, fleet AI) differs from display drivers and ADAS SoCs, so the transmission is unconfirmed.
findings.independence: Mobileye's Q3 2026 release and coverage (https://www.securities.io/mobileye-narrows-2026-revenue-guidance-as-q3-sales-slip-2/) is a different company and document, pointing the same way more mildly.

findings.finding: Long-only holders added through Q3. T. Rowe Price went from 2,598,863 shares (5.9%, 2026-06-30) to 3,369,033 (7.6%, 2026-09-30) per the 13G/A filed 2026-11-16, and Vanguard Portfolio Management reported 7.04% (13G/A, 2026-10-30).
findings.why_not_priced: Stale: the position is as of Sep 30, before the sector crash. Filed as a small sourced fact on the holder base.
findings.independence: The earlier T. Rowe 13G (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1280263/000008025526000550/primary_doc.xml) is the comparison point, from the same filer.

findings.finding: On the print day Morgan Stanley cut its price target to $70 from $96 and kept its Overweight rating (reported by MarketBeat and Investing.com, though no Fly headline was found). The stock fell about 10-12% intraday to a 52-week low of about $48.1. The cut signals sell-side trimming into the print, while $70 still sits about 43% above spot.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced by today's drop. The note's content (Q4/memory or multiple) is not visible.
findings.independence: Investing.com preview reports the same cut (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/ambarella-earnings-on-deck-as-ai-chip-transition-faces-test-93CH-5048515). The same day's chip selloff is a confounder.

outside_window.finding: The CV7 (4nm) ramp, the X7 standalone AI accelerator and the Capgemini/Macnica channel agreements (each sized at about $500M of opportunity) are multi-quarter revenue drivers that will not show in this window beyond commentary.

baseline_tension: The Q4-memory negative runs against the upside-paid skew (-6.9) and a stock already at its 52-week low, but with the name's own 6-of-7-down reaction history. The 27% run-down is mostly the sector, so it does not by itself mean the bad news is priced. Net, p_up sits only slightly below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (skew and short interest): the Q4-guide negative goes against a -6.9 upside-paid skew with about 10.5% short; shrunk from -2.5 to -2.0, and p_up moved from 45 to 46.
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Q3 beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5 because this name has sold its beats.
Rule 5 (positioning and unexplained drawdowns): the sector-drawdown positioning finding is an inference about reversion, not a document; cut from +1.5 to +1.0.
Rule 9 (net of the rest of the company): the auto-peer proxy is a minority segment against growing IoT; cut from -0.7 to -0.5.
Minor trims: Arlo proxy +0.5 to +0.4 (not confirmed as a current customer); inventory -0.5 to -0.4; Morgan Stanley cut -0.3 to -0.2 (priced today).
Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar was already resolved to two agreeing sources plus the guide midpoint, so no cap was applied.
